dialogue.text: Konnichiwa, Japan is a monot, misa dese, kenky dese car, this is the 4th episode for absolute beginners, hope you enjoy it.
dialogue.zh: 你好，日本是單調的，misa dese，kenky dese car，這是給完全初學者的第四集，希望你喜歡。
dialogue.ja: こんにちは、日本は単調ですが、misa dese、kenky dese car、これは初心者向けの第4話です。楽しんでくださいね。
dialogue.local: Hello, Japan is a monot, misa dese, kenky dese car, this is the 4th episode for absolute beginners, hope you enjoy it.
dialogue.en: Hello, Japan is a monot, misa dese, kenky dese car, this is the 4th episode for absolute beginners, hope you enjoy it.

dialogue.text: So in the previous episode we learned how to negate a noun, do you remember how? 4th informal speech you put jai nai after noun, right?
dialogue.zh: 在上一集我們學了如何否定名詞，你還記得嗎？在非正式語氣中，名詞後面加 jai nai，對吧？
dialogue.ja: 前回は名詞の否定の仕方を学びましたね。覚えていますか？カジュアルな話し方では名詞の後に「じゃない」をつけますよね？
dialogue.local: In the previous episode, we learned how to negate a noun. In informal speech, you put 'jai nai' after the noun, right?
dialogue.en: In the previous episode, we learned how to negate a noun. In informal speech, you put 'jai nai' after the noun, right?

dialogue.text: But 4th formal speech you put jai arimasen after noun, for example do you remember how to say watch?
dialogue.zh: 但正式語氣中，名詞後面要加 jai arimasen。比如你還記得怎麼說手錶嗎？
dialogue.ja: しかし、丁寧な話し方では名詞の後に「じゃありません」をつけます。例えば、時計の言い方を覚えていますか？
dialogue.local: In formal speech, you put 'jai arimasen' after the noun. For example, do you remember how to say watch?
dialogue.en: In formal speech, you put 'jai arimasen' after the noun. For example, do you remember how to say watch?

dialogue.text: It's okay, okay, how do you say this is a watch, koreva, koreva, this is not a watch, koreva jai arimasen.
dialogue.zh: 沒關係，這是手錶怎麼說？koreva，koreva，這不是手錶怎麼說？koreva jai arimasen。
dialogue.ja: 大丈夫です。「これは時計です」はどう言いますか？「これは時計です」。そして「これは時計じゃありません」は？
dialogue.local: It's okay. How do you say 'this is a watch'? Koreva. And 'this is not a watch'? Koreva jai arimasen.
dialogue.en: It's okay. How do you say 'this is a watch'? Koreva. And 'this is not a watch'? Koreva jai arimasen.

dialogue.text: Today we are going to learn more adjectives, so I already introduced some adjectives even in the first episode, for example you guys know the word, kii, kawaii, what about hot?
dialogue.zh: 今天我們要學更多形容詞，我在第一集就介紹過一些形容詞，比如你們知道的詞，kii、kawaii，那熱怎麼說？
dialogue.ja: 今日はもっと形容詞を学びます。第一話でもいくつか紹介しましたね。例えば「きい」「かわいい」。では「暑い」は？
dialogue.local: Today we will learn more adjectives. I already introduced some in the first episode, like 'kii', 'kawaii'. What about 'hot'?
dialogue.en: Today we will learn more adjectives. I already introduced some in the first episode, like 'kii', 'kawaii'. What about 'hot'?

dialogue.text: It is very hot in Montreal, what you need to know before it is that we have two types of adjectives on the is called easjective and another one is not adjective.
dialogue.zh: 蒙特利爾非常熱，你需要知道的是形容詞有兩種類型，一種叫做い形容詞，另一種不是形容詞。
dialogue.ja: モントリオールはとても暑いです。知っておくべきことは、形容詞には「い形容詞」と「な形容詞」の2種類があるということです。
dialogue.local: It is very hot in Montreal. You need to know there are two types of adjectives: i-adjectives and na-adjectives.
dialogue.en: It is very hot in Montreal. You need to know there are two types of adjectives: i-adjectives and na-adjectives.

dialogue.text: Let's take a look. Chris, I will introduce easjectives. Carla, ee, cute. Add to the hot, erosai, noisy, but you can use like chop-up.
dialogue.zh: 我們來看看。Chris，我會介紹い形容詞。Carla，ee，可愛。還有熱、うるさい、吵鬧，但你也可以用像 chop-up 這樣的詞。
dialogue.ja: 見てみましょう。クリス、い形容詞を紹介します。カワイイ、暑い、うるさいなどです。ただし「chop-up」のような言葉も使えます。
dialogue.local: Let's look. Chris, I will introduce i-adjectives: kawaii, atsui (hot), urusai (noisy). You can also use words like chop-up.
dialogue.en: Let's look. Chris, I will introduce i-adjectives: kawaii, atsui (hot), urusai (noisy). You can also use words like chop-up.

dialogue.text: Okay, so here you look at the ending. All of them have easjective. That's why it's called easjective.
dialogue.zh: 好，這裡看詞尾，全部都是い形容詞，所以叫い形容詞。
dialogue.ja: はい、ここで語尾を見てください。全部い形容詞だから、い形容詞と呼ばれます。
dialogue.local: Okay, look at the endings. All have i-adjective endings, so they are called i-adjectives.
dialogue.en: Okay, look at the endings. All have i-adjective endings, so they are called i-adjectives.

dialogue.text: So this Carla, ea lot of people miss one ea and they just say Carla, but it's actually Carla, ea, longed ball.
dialogue.zh: 這個Carla，很多人會漏掉一個い，只說Carla，但其實是Carlaい，長音符號。
dialogue.ja: この「カワラ」、多くの人は「い」を省略して「カワラ」と言いますが、正しくは「カワライ」です。
dialogue.local: This 'Carla', many people miss the 'i' and just say 'Carla', but actually it's 'Carla i' with a long vowel.
dialogue.en: This 'Carla', many people miss the 'i' and just say 'Carla', but actually it's 'Carla i' with a long vowel.

dialogue.text: Carla, ea, this one is very easy. You can just put in a construction x, y, y, this. For example, if I want to say docs are cute, then enua, Carla, ea, that's enua, that's why it is.
dialogue.zh: Carlaい，這個很簡單。你可以用結構 x は y です。比如說狗很可愛，就是 inu wa kawaii desu。
dialogue.ja: 「カワライ」は簡単です。文の構造は「XはYです」。例えば「犬はかわいいです」と言います。
dialogue.local: Carla i is easy. Use the structure 'X wa Y desu'. For example, 'Dogs are cute' is 'Inu wa kawaii desu'.
dialogue.en: Carla i is easy. Use the structure 'X wa Y desu'. For example, 'Dogs are cute' is 'Inu wa kawaii desu'.

dialogue.text: What about this tea is hot? Tea is au ciao. In me, say au ciao, we usually refer to green tea. Not always. So if you want to say black tea, say ciao ciao, which actually means red tea.
dialogue.zh: 這茶很熱怎麼說？茶是あつい。通常說あつい是指綠茶，不一定。黑茶說こうちゃ，意思是紅茶。
dialogue.ja: 「このお茶は暑い」は「あついです」。普通は緑茶を指しますが、必ずしもそうではありません。紅茶は「こうちゃ」と言います。
dialogue.local: How to say 'This tea is hot'? Tea is 'atsui'. Usually 'atsui' refers to green tea, not always. Black tea is 'koucha', meaning red tea.
dialogue.en: How to say 'This tea is hot'? Tea is 'atsui'. Usually 'atsui' refers to green tea, not always. Black tea is 'koucha', meaning red tea.

dialogue.text: If I want to keep it the word very, I just put it in front of it. I'm not sure why I can English. I say conno au ciao a totemo a toi des.
dialogue.zh: 如果要說非常熱，我會放在前面。我不確定為什麼英文是這樣，我說このお茶はとても暑いです。
dialogue.ja: 「とても」を使いたい場合は、形容詞の前に置きます。例えば「このお茶はとても暑いです」と言います。
dialogue.local: If I want to say very hot, I put 'totemo' before it. For example, 'Kono ocha wa totemo atsui desu'.
dialogue.en: If I want to say very hot, I put 'totemo' before it. For example, 'Kono ocha wa totemo atsui desu'.

dialogue.text: We often say totemo instead of totemo, very small totemo, it's just more like very hot. So it's a bit slightly more clocquil.
dialogue.zh: 我們常說とても而不是とても，非常小的とても，更像是非常熱，所以稍微更口語。
dialogue.ja: よく「とても」と言いますが、もっと口語的に「とっても」とも言います。意味は「とても暑い」と同じです。
dialogue.local: We often say 'tottemo' instead of 'totemo'. It's more casual but means very hot.
dialogue.en: We often say 'tottemo' instead of 'totemo'. It's more casual but means very hot.

dialogue.text: So when you have to write an essay, for example, just stick to totemo without to, or when you're just speaking generally, it's fine, it gives a totemo.
dialogue.zh: 寫作文時，還是用とても，不要用とっても。平常說話用都可以。
dialogue.ja: 作文を書く時は「とても」を使いましょう。話す時は「とっても」でも大丈夫です。
dialogue.local: When writing essays, use 'totemo'. In casual speech, 'tottemo' is fine.
dialogue.en: When writing essays, use 'totemo'. In casual speech, 'tottemo' is fine.

dialogue.text: More adjectives, for example, samui, samui, call. How do you say winter in Canada is called? We say, speaking of kambos, winter, it is called, then kana dana, who you are, samui des, kana dana, who you are, samui des.
dialogue.zh: 更多形容詞，比如寒い。加拿大的冬天怎麼說？我們說冬天是冬、寒いです。
dialogue.ja: 他の形容詞も紹介します。例えば「寒い」。カナダの冬は「冬」と言います。「寒いです」と言います。
dialogue.local: More adjectives: for example, 'samui' (cold). Winter in Canada is called 'fuyu'. We say 'samui desu'.
dialogue.en: More adjectives: for example, 'samui' (cold). Winter in Canada is called 'fuyu'. We say 'samui desu'.

dialogue.text: What about the word interesting? Do you remember face white? Almost here I, almost here I. So how do we say this movie is interesting? Conno au ciao, almost here I des.
dialogue.zh: 有趣怎麼說？你記得面白い嗎？這部電影很有趣怎麼說？この映画は面白いです。
dialogue.ja: 「面白い」は覚えていますか？この映画は面白いですと言います。
dialogue.local: What about 'interesting'? Do you remember 'omoshiroi'? This movie is interesting: 'Kono eiga wa omoshiroi desu'.
dialogue.en: What about 'interesting'? Do you remember 'omoshiroi'? This movie is interesting: 'Kono eiga wa omoshiroi desu'.

dialogue.text: For I introduce not adjectives, I would like to show you how to you say, I like something, la, la, gah, skydess.
dialogue.zh: 接下來介紹な形容詞，先教你怎麼說我喜歡某物，la, la, gah, skydess。
dialogue.ja: な形容詞を紹介します。まず「好きです」の使い方を教えます。
dialogue.local: Now I introduce na-adjectives. First, how to say 'I like something': 'X ga suki desu'.
dialogue.en: Now I introduce na-adjectives. First, how to say 'I like something': 'X ga suki desu'.

dialogue.text: For example, I like dogs, enuga, skydess. I like picketru. I like missus enbe, missas en sega, skydess.
dialogue.zh: 例如，我喜歡狗，inu ga suki desu。我喜歡皮卡丘。我喜歡蜜蜂，missa en sega suki desu。
dialogue.ja: 例えば「犬が好きです」「ピカチュウが好きです」「ミッサが好きです」と言います。
dialogue.local: For example, 'I like dogs' is 'Inu ga suki desu'. 'I like Pikachu'. 'I like Missa'.
dialogue.en: For example, 'I like dogs' is 'Inu ga suki desu'. 'I like Pikachu'. 'I like Missa'.

dialogue.text: I'll be really happy if you leave that comment, missas en sega, skydess. I like cats, neko, gah, skydess.
dialogue.zh: 如果你留言我會很開心，我喜歡蜜蜂。我喜歡貓，neko ga suki desu。
dialogue.ja: コメントを残してくれると嬉しいです。「猫が好きです」と言います。
dialogue.local: I will be happy if you leave a comment. 'I like cats' is 'Neko ga suki desu'.
dialogue.en: I will be happy if you leave a comment. 'I like cats' is 'Neko ga suki desu'.

dialogue.text: Why did I introduce this one? I will explain this gut particle in the next lesson, but let's focus on this suki first.
dialogue.zh: 為什麼介紹這個？我會在下一課解釋這個助詞，現在先專注於suki。
dialogue.ja: なぜこれを紹介したかというと、次のレッスンで助詞について説明しますが、まずは「好き」に注目しましょう。
dialogue.local: Why did I introduce this? I will explain the particle next lesson. Let's focus on 'suki' now.
dialogue.en: Why did I introduce this? I will explain the particle next lesson. Let's focus on 'suki' now.

dialogue.text: Okay, so suki is actually a not adjective, but you can't see not anywhere, because it's hiding.
dialogue.zh: 好，suki其實是な形容詞，但你看不到な，因為它藏起來了。
dialogue.ja: 「好き」は実はな形容詞ですが、「な」が見えません。隠れているからです。
dialogue.local: 'Suki' is actually a na-adjective, but you don't see the 'na' because it's hidden.
dialogue.en: 'Suki' is actually a na-adjective, but you don't see the 'na' because it's hidden.

dialogue.text: Now adjective is so good at hide and seek. This suki nah, the dictionary form is actually suki nah.
dialogue.zh: な形容詞很會玩捉迷藏，suki的字典形是suki na。
dialogue.ja: な形容詞はかくれんぼが得意です。「好きな」が辞書形です。
dialogue.local: Na-adjectives are good at hide and seek. The dictionary form of 'suki' is 'suki na'.
dialogue.en: Na-adjectives are good at hide and seek. The dictionary form of 'suki' is 'suki na'.

dialogue.text: The thing is negative, it's kind of weird. When there is a noun calling noun, you have to leave this noun.
dialogue.zh: 否定形有點奇怪，當有名詞修飾時，要保留這個な。
dialogue.ja: 否定形は少し変です。名詞を修飾するときは「な」を残します。
dialogue.local: The negative form is a bit weird. When modifying a noun, you keep the 'na'.
dialogue.en: The negative form is a bit weird. When modifying a noun, you keep the 'na'.

dialogue.text: So suki nah, for example, suki nah, hon, skydess, hon, with mean favor. It's suki this, it's actually not a verb, but it actually means likable.
dialogue.zh: 例如，好きな本が好きです。hon是書，意思是喜歡。suki不是動詞，但意思是喜歡的。
dialogue.ja: 例えば「好きな本が好きです」。「本」は書物の意味です。「好き」は動詞ではなく、好ましいという意味です。
dialogue.local: For example, 'suki na hon ga suki desu'. 'Hon' means book. 'Suki' is not a verb but means likable.
dialogue.en: For example, 'suki na hon ga suki desu'. 'Hon' means book. 'Suki' is not a verb but means likable.

dialogue.text: Something is likable or something is favor. So for example, f 50 shares of good air, wah, wah, suki nah, hon, des, or hari, pok, bah, wah, wah, suki nah, hon, des.
dialogue.zh: 某物是可喜歡的或受歡迎的。例如、f 50 shares of good air，wah wah，suki na hon des。
dialogue.ja: 何かが好ましいという意味です。例えば「好きな本です」と言います。
dialogue.local: Something is likable or favored. For example, 'suki na hon desu'.
dialogue.en: Something is likable or favored. For example, 'suki na hon desu'.

dialogue.text: So this not adjective, remember, when there is a noun calling, so you use like favor or then you have to leave this noun, but when there is no noun calling, because this is actually a verb, then you cannot put noun.
dialogue.zh: 這是な形容詞，當有名詞修飾時要保留な，沒名詞修飾時不能放名詞。
dialogue.ja: これはな形容詞です。名詞を修飾するときは「な」を使いますが、修飾しないときは使いません。
dialogue.local: This is a na-adjective. When modifying a noun, use 'na'. Without noun, don't use 'na'.
dialogue.en: This is a na-adjective. When modifying a noun, use 'na'. Without noun, don't use 'na'.

dialogue.text: I will show you more examples, kam tana means easy. If you use some textbooks, it says yasashi, but never use yasashi as easy.
dialogue.zh: 我會給你更多例子，かんたんな意思是簡單。有些教材用やさしい，但不要用やさしい表示簡單。
dialogue.ja: もっと例を見せます。「かんたん」は「簡単」という意味です。教科書によっては「やさしい」と書いてありますが、簡単の意味では使わないでください。
dialogue.local: More examples: 'kantan' means easy. Some textbooks say 'yasashii', but don't use 'yasashii' for easy.
dialogue.en: More examples: 'kantan' means easy. Some textbooks say 'yasashii', but don't use 'yasashii' for easy.

dialogue.text: It's just wait, wait, two formats. If you want to sound naked, use kam tana, because yasashi can also mean kind.
dialogue.zh: 有兩種用法。如果想說簡單，用かんたん，因為やさしい也可以表示親切。
dialogue.ja: 2つの使い方があります。簡単と言いたい時は「かんたん」を使いましょう。「やさしい」は親切の意味もあります。
dialogue.local: There are two forms. To say easy, use 'kantan' because 'yasashii' can also mean kind.
dialogue.en: There are two forms. To say easy, use 'kantan' because 'yasashii' can also mean kind.

dialogue.text: And one means people here, the word yasashi, we immediately think of yasashi as kind.
dialogue.zh: 這裡的やさしい，我們會立刻想到親切的意思。
dialogue.ja: 「やさしい」は人に対して親切という意味をすぐに連想します。
dialogue.local: The word 'yasashii' often immediately means kind to people.
dialogue.en: The word 'yasashii' often immediately means kind to people.

dialogue.text: For example, if I want to say easy kam t, then I would say kam tana, kang ji, so there is noun calling, so we don't drop nah.
dialogue.zh: 例如，我想說簡單的漢字，我會說かんたんな漢字，有名詞修飾所以不省略な。
dialogue.ja: 例えば「簡単な漢字」と言います。名詞を修飾するので「な」を省略しません。
dialogue.local: For example, 'easy kanji' is 'kantan na kanji'. Since noun follows, don't drop 'na'.
dialogue.en: For example, 'easy kanji' is 'kantan na kanji'. Since noun follows, don't drop 'na'.

dialogue.text: So for example, if I want to say this is an easy kang ji, then I say karewa, kam tana, kang ji des, right?
dialogue.zh: 所以如果我想說這是簡單的漢字，我會說これはかんたんな漢字です，對吧？
dialogue.ja: だから「これは簡単な漢字です」と言いますね？
dialogue.local: So if I want to say 'This is an easy kanji', I say 'Kore wa kantan na kanji desu', right?
dialogue.en: So if I want to say 'This is an easy kanji', I say 'Kore wa kantan na kanji desu', right?

dialogue.text: But for example, if I want to say this is easy, so there is no noun calling, then I say kon kang jiwa, kam tana, kam tana, kam tana,
dialogue.zh: 但如果我想說這很簡單，沒有名詞修飾，我會說これはかんたんです。
dialogue.ja: しかし「これは簡単です」と言いたい場合、名詞がないので「な」は使いません。
dialogue.local: But if I want to say 'This is easy' with no noun, I say 'Kore wa kantan desu'.
dialogue.en: But if I want to say 'This is easy' with no noun, I say 'Kore wa kantan desu'.

dialogue.text: So you can remember, I think, I can say the next one is kide nah, kide nah, which means beautiful and also clean.
dialogue.zh: 你可以記住下一個是きれいな，意思是漂亮也可以是乾淨。
dialogue.ja: 次は「きれいな」です。意味は美しい、そしてきれい（清潔）です。
dialogue.local: Next is 'kirei na', which means beautiful and also clean.
dialogue.en: Next is 'kirei na', which means beautiful and also clean.

dialogue.text: So if I want to say beautiful, beautiful, beautiful woman, then I say kide nah, what about clean room? What for room is kaya?
dialogue.zh: 如果我想說漂亮的女人，我會說きれいな女。房間是へや，乾淨的房間怎麼說？
dialogue.ja: 美しい女性は「きれいな女の人」と言います。部屋は「へや」です。きれいな部屋は？
dialogue.local: If I want to say beautiful woman, I say 'kirei na onna'. Room is 'heya'. How to say clean room?
dialogue.en: If I want to say beautiful woman, I say 'kirei na onna'. Room is 'heya'. How to say clean room?

dialogue.text: You can remember like a British woman comes into your room and says kaya, kide nah, kaya, clean room.
dialogue.zh: 你可以想像一位英國女士進你的房間說きれいな部屋，表示乾淨的房間。
dialogue.ja: イギリスの女性が部屋に入って「きれいな部屋」と言うイメージです。
dialogue.local: Imagine a British woman entering your room and saying 'kirei na heya' meaning clean room.
dialogue.en: Imagine a British woman entering your room and saying 'kirei na heya' meaning clean room.

dialogue.text: It can mean beautiful room, it's really all about context. Kaya nah, kide nah, kita, but for example, if I want to say something or someone is beautiful, then there is no noun calling, it becomes something well, kide des.
dialogue.zh: 它也可以是漂亮的房間，這要看語境。きれいな、きれいな、きた。但如果沒名詞修飾，就說きれいです。
dialogue.ja: 文脈によっては美しい部屋の意味にもなります。名詞がない場合は「きれいです」と言います。
dialogue.local: It can mean beautiful room depending on context. Without noun, say 'kirei desu'.
dialogue.en: It can mean beautiful room depending on context. Without noun, say 'kirei desu'.

dialogue.text: So when you look at kide des, you might think this is actually an e-objective, but it's not, it actually is not addictive.
dialogue.zh: 看きれいです時，你可能以為是い形容詞，但不是，它不是形容詞。
dialogue.ja: 「きれいです」を見るとい形容詞に見えますが、実は違います。な形容詞です。
dialogue.local: When you see 'kirei desu', you might think it's an i-adjective, but it's not; it's a na-adjective.
dialogue.en: When you see 'kirei desu', you might think it's an i-adjective, but it's not; it's a na-adjective.

dialogue.text: This is very very common mistake, so don't forget, kide is actually kide nah, not adjective, it's just there is no noun calling, okay?
dialogue.zh: 這是很常見的錯誤，別忘了きれいはきれいな，な形容詞，只是沒有名詞修飾。
dialogue.ja: これはよくある間違いです。忘れないでください。「きれい」は「きれいな」で、な形容詞です。名詞がないだけです。
dialogue.local: This is a common mistake. Remember 'kirei' is 'kirei na', a na-adjective, just no noun follows.
dialogue.en: This is a common mistake. Remember 'kirei' is 'kirei na', a na-adjective, just no noun follows.

dialogue.text: So if I want to say you're beautiful, but I don't want to say the word another, because it's rude, so I'd say the person's name and is beautiful, right?
dialogue.zh: 如果我想說你很漂亮，但不想說你這個詞，因為不禮貌，我會說名字加上漂亮，對吧？
dialogue.ja: 「あなたはきれいです」と言いたくない時は、名前を言って「きれいです」と言いますね？
dialogue.local: If I want to say 'You are beautiful' but avoid 'anata' because it's rude, I say the person's name plus 'kirei desu'.
dialogue.en: If I want to say 'You are beautiful' but avoid 'anata' because it's rude, I say the person's name plus 'kirei desu'.

dialogue.text: So I'm talking to the girl called Haruka, then Harukawa, kide des, Harukawa, kide des, you're beautiful, Haruka, fans on the Japanese girl, but I think a lot of girls prefer to be called kawaii,
dialogue.zh: 我對一位叫Haruka的女孩說，Haruka wa kirei desu，你很漂亮。日本女生粉絲，但很多女生喜歡被叫kawaii。
dialogue.ja: 「はるかはきれいです」と言います。日本の女の子のファンですが、多くの女の子は「かわいい」と呼ばれるのが好きです。
dialogue.local: Talking to a girl named Haruka: 'Haruka wa kirei desu' means 'You are beautiful, Haruka'. Many girls prefer 'kawaii'.
dialogue.en: Talking to a girl named Haruka: 'Haruka wa kirei desu' means 'You are beautiful, Haruka'. Many girls prefer 'kawaii'.

dialogue.text: But it really depends on their age as well. So young girls prefer kawaii, but maybe like moms, I mean, you know, if there is a milk, you might say kide, not kawaii, sorry for the weird example,
dialogue.zh: 但這也看年齡，年輕女孩喜歡kawaii，媽媽可能說kirei，不是kawaii，抱歉奇怪的例子。
dialogue.ja: 年齢にもよります。若い女の子は「かわいい」が好きですが、お母さん世代は「きれい」と言うかもしれません。変な例でごめんなさい。
dialogue.local: It depends on age. Young girls like 'kawaii', moms might say 'kirei'. Sorry for the weird example.
dialogue.en: It depends on age. Young girls like 'kawaii', moms might say 'kirei'. Sorry for the weird example.

dialogue.text: So if you say clean room, it's kide nah haa, right? But if I want to say this room is beautiful, then I say kawaii haa, what? kide des, kawaii haa, kide des, but in informal space there is no des, right?
dialogue.zh: 說乾淨的房間是きれいなへや，對吧？說漂亮的房間是かわいいへや？きれいです，かわいいへや，きれいです。非正式語氣沒有です。
dialogue.ja: 「きれいな部屋」と言いますね？「かわいい部屋」？「きれいです」「かわいい部屋」「きれいです」。カジュアルな場面では「です」はありません。
dialogue.local: Clean room is 'kirei na heya'. Beautiful room? 'Kawaii heya'? 'Kirei desu'. In informal speech, no 'desu'.
dialogue.en: Clean room is 'kirei na heya'. Beautiful room? 'Kawaii heya'? 'Kirei desu'. In informal speech, no 'desu'.

dialogue.text: But still, there will be no nah, so when you want to say oh wow, Haruka, are beautiful, you don't want to say what is beautiful, then you can say kide, so it's here, that's here really beautiful view, you say Haruka, you don't say kide nah, because there is no nah point.
dialogue.zh: 但還是沒有な，所以想說哇，Haruka很漂亮，不會說きれいな，會說きれい，這裡是很美的風景，你說Haruka，不說きれいな，因為沒な的用處。
dialogue.ja: でも「な」は使いません。例えば「はるか、きれい！」と言います。「きれいな」は使いません。ここは本当にきれいな景色です。「はるか」と言う時は「きれいな」は不要です。
dialogue.local: Still no 'na'. To say 'Wow, Haruka is beautiful', say 'Haruka kirei'. Don't say 'kirei na' because no noun follows.
dialogue.en: Still no 'na'. To say 'Wow, Haruka is beautiful', say 'Haruka kirei'. Don't say 'kirei na' because no noun follows.
